objective: Leadership approves a short AI policy that sets direction and is reviewed on a fixed cycle
evidence_examples: Approved policy with version history|Minutes showing annual review

objective: Named people are accountable for AI risk and each AI system has a business owner
evidence_examples: RACI chart|Role descriptions|Owner field completed in the inventory

objective: The organisation tracks which AI rules apply to it and when they apply
evidence_examples: Register of obligations with dates and owners|Quarterly review note

objective: The scope of AI governance is written down and resourced
evidence_examples: Scope statement|Budget or time allocation approved by the sponsor

objective: Leadership sets what AI should achieve and how much risk is acceptable
evidence_examples: Risk appetite statement|Objectives with measures and dates

objective: People who build buy or use AI have the knowledge their role needs
Staff and others can raise concerns about AI safely and get a response
evidence_examples: Published reporting route|Log of concerns with outcomes

objective: AI governance records are controlled versioned and retained
It is clear what is communicated about AI to whom and by whom
Governance is checked independently and leadership reviews results
evidence_examples: Audit plan and reports|Management review minutes

objective: Problems lead to tracked fixes and the system gets better over time
evidence_examples: Corrective action log|Closed actions with evidence

objective: Decisions about higher-risk AI draw on varied viewpoints and independent challenge
evidence_examples: Review panel membership|Record of independent challenge

objective: Every AI system in use or planned is recorded with an owner and status
evidence_examples: Inventory with all fields completed|Quarterly reconciliation with procurement

objective: Each system is assigned an EU risk tier and the organisation's role (provider or deployer) is recorded
evidence_examples: Classification rationale in the inventory|Review when the use changes

objective: New use cases are screened against the list of banned practices before work starts
evidence_examples: Screening record on each intake form

objective: Data tools computing and skills each system relies on are recorded
evidence_examples: System card sections on data and infrastructure

objective: Systems are withdrawn safely and their data and access are dealt with
evidence_examples: Retirement checklist|Evidence of access removal and data disposal

objective: A consistent method scores AI risks and is applied at planned points
evidence_examples: Written method with scales|Risk register entries

control_name: Risk treatment and residual risk acceptance
objective: Risks are treated and the remaining risk is accepted by someone with authority
The effects of a system on people and society are assessed before launch and on change

control_name: Fundamental rights and data protection check
objective: Where required a fundamental rights assessment is linked to the data protection impact assessment
evidence_examples: DPIA reference in the impact assessment|FRIA where Art 27 applies

objective: People affected by a system are consulted and feedback changes decisions
evidence_examples: Consultation notes|Changes made as a result

objective: Results are checked with domain experts and field data feeds back into decisions
Material changes to a system trigger review before release
Intended use and limits are specified before build or purchase
Systems are tested against stated requirements in realistic conditions
Outputs are checked for unfair differences between groups where people are affected
evidence_examples: Fairness test results|Documented thresholds and actions

objective: Systems are tested for misuse manipulation and loss of service
A named approver decides whether a system goes live based on evidence
Live systems are monitored for drift errors and misuse
evidence_examples: Monitoring dashboard or report|Review cadence in the system card

objective: Events needed to investigate outcomes are recorded and kept for a set period
Each system has current documentation describing design data testing and limits
Trained people can understand intervene and override where the system affects people
There is a tested manual fallback if the system fails or must be switched off
Data used to train test or run a system is suitable and its limits are known
evidence_examples: Data quality checks|Data description in the system card

objective: The source and rights to use data are known and recorded
evidence_examples: Data source register|Licence or contract evidence

objective: Personal data use in AI is reviewed against data protection duties

control_name: Acceptable use rules and approved tools
objective: Staff know which AI tools are approved and what may be entered into them
evidence_examples: Acceptable use policy|Approved tools list|Acknowledgement records

control_name: Disclosure of AI interaction and content
objective: People are told when they deal with AI and AI-generated content is marked where required

control_name: Information for affected people and workers
objective: Affected people and workers get meaningful information about AI-assisted decisions
People can challenge AI-assisted outcomes and get a human review
evidence_examples: Appeal procedure|Log of appeals and outcomes

objective: AI suppliers are assessed for risk before purchase and at renewal
evidence_examples: Completed vendor review|Request for model information

objective: Contracts say who is responsible for what including incidents data and audit
Supplier performance and changes are monitored and exit is planned
Where the organisation supplies AI to customers their needs and the shared duties are covered
AI incidents are logged triaged investigated and closed with lessons recorded
Reportable incidents reach providers and authorities within required time limits
Providers of AI systems collect and review performance data after release

control_name: Quality management system for high-risk systems
objective: Providers of high-risk systems run a documented quality management system
Providers complete conformity steps before placing a high-risk system on the market
